sandbox.title: Security
sandbox.description: Ares 2 sandboxes the student code while the tests run. Java exercises start with it activated; deactivating it switches off the sandbox and everything the security policy configures for the tests.
sandbox.subtitle: Programming Exercise Security Framework
sandbox.frameworkVersionHelp: The Ares release the tests run with, pinned in the build file of the tests repository. Newer releases support more policy settings and fix sandbox issues, so new exercises use the latest one. Choose an older release only if the exercise must keep behaving exactly as it did with it.

unsupportedReason.UNEVALUABLE_ARGUMENTS: {{ location }}: A @Policy annotation uses an expression instead of a literal value.
unsupportedReason.POLICY_NOT_ON_TOP_LEVEL_TYPE: {{ location }}: A @Policy annotation is placed on a method, a field or a nested type instead of the test class.
unsupportedReason.POLICY_ON_ANNOTATION_TYPE: {{ location }}: A @Policy annotation is placed on an annotation type.
unsupportedReason.MULTIPLE_TOP_LEVEL_TYPES: {{ location }}: The file declares more than one top-level type that is a test class or carries a @Policy annotation.
unsupportedReason.TESTS_IN_NESTED_TYPE: {{ location }}: Tests or Ares annotations are inside a nested type.
unsupportedReason.TEST_CLASS_WITHOUT_POLICY: {{ location }}: A test class uses the Ares sandbox without its own @Policy annotation.
unsupportedReason.TEST_CLASS_WITHOUT_ARES: {{ location }}: A test class does not register the Ares sandbox through @Public, @Hidden, @PublicTest or @HiddenTest.
unsupportedReason.ARES_1: {{ location }}: The tests use Ares 1, whose own sandbox keeps running.
unsupportedReason.NO_ARES_2: {{ location }}: The tests do not use Ares 2.
unsupportedReason.NO_ARES_VERSION_PINNED: {{ location }}: The build file does not pin an Ares version.
unsupportedReason.ARES_VERSION_IN_MAVEN_PROFILE: {{ location }}: A Maven profile pins the Ares version, so the version the build uses depends on the active profiles.

deactivateConfirmation.message: Deactivating creates a commit in the tests repository that deletes the security policy with all its settings, and the template and solution builds run again. This switches off the sandbox for student code and everything the policy configures for the tests, such as hidden-test scheduling, output handling and failure reporting. Ares features the tests use directly, such as @StrictTimeout, keep working. Hidden tests are then protected only by the test visibility settings of Artemis, not by Ares. Activating again restores the last policy from the repository history, or generates a default policy if none is found.
deactivateConfirmation.aresLibraryStays: The tests also use other parts of Ares ({{ apis }}), so the Ares library stays in the build file.
